focal_entities.audience: the user approving the README at the design sign-off, and whoever makes the architecture and the tool to it

goal_orientation.purpose: approving how a newcomer installs the tool and uses it, and building the architecture and the tool to what it says

goal_orientation.serves: AC2: Run on a folder with the option that tells it to move, the tool moves each file directly in it that is of a known kind into that kind's folder inside it, made where missing, under the same name and with the same contents, and prints the same lines as AC1. The kinds' folders are Images (such as jpg, png, gif, heic, webp, svg), Documents (such as pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, txt, md, csv), Archives (such as zip, tar, gz, 7z, rar), Installers (such as dmg, pkg, deb, rpm, AppImage), Audio (such as mp3, wav, m4a) and Videos (such as mp4, mov, mkv); the full list of extensions of each is settled in the design.
AC10: The README says how to install the tool and how to use it on macOS and Linux, and a user following it alone installs the tool, lists the planned moves, moves the files and undoes the move.

constraints.decision: How the tool is made and installed: The tool is one Python 3 program in a single file, using only Python's standard library; it is installed by downloading that file into ~/.local/bin and making it runnable, on macOS and Linux alike, with nothing else to install. Its tests run by one command with what Python itself provides.

License and the places of fuller use and of changes: The tool is offered under the MIT license, at organize-downloads/LICENSE. Fuller use is written in organize-downloads/docs/usage.md and the changes of each version in organize-downloads/CHANGELOG.md, both still to be made with the tool; the README's Development links to organize-downloads/docs/architecture.md, made by T2.
Copyright line of the license: The MIT license at organize-downloads/LICENSE reads "Copyright (c) 2026 lovaizu".

constraints.chosen: The README is approved at the design stage as what the build makes, its download address kept as written, and its installation and Example are tried by a first user only once the build stage has made the tool and put it on main, so at this stage B-4 is judged by whether the steps, followed once the tool is there, give what they say: the tool does not exist before the build, the plan's next stage, where rn adds the task that makes it
organize-downloads/LICENSE is made with this work: it needs nothing from the tool, so the README's license link opens once the README is approved

organize-downloads/docs/usage.md and organize-downloads/CHANGELOG.md are made with the tool in the build stage, and at this stage the README's links to them and to docs/architecture.md, made by T2, name where they will be: they can only be written once the tool exists, as the decision on their places says

constraints.decision: How t1.1 ends: The README is taken as it is at the design stage; B-4, B-5 and B-8 of the README checklist, which need the tool and the linked pages, are checked at the build stage, by a first user installing from the README's address and following its Example once the tool, docs/usage.md and CHANGELOG.md are on main and docs/architecture.md is made.
